strengths: The paper addresses an identifiable audience in program representation learning and binary analysis. Transferring information from paired source code and comments into an LLVM encoder is a useful research direction.

The reported results are promising across several tasks: POJ-104 MAP reaches 43.78 versus 39.99 for CodeBERT; function-name accuracy reaches 33.41 versus 29.41 for RoBERTa; summarization BLEU-4 reaches 34.36 versus 32.43 for GraphCodeBERT.

The manuscript includes component ablations, a CodeT5 extension, and positive and negative examples. The overview diagram communicates the broad training pipeline, and the data-availability statement provides a Zenodo link for code, datasets, and configurations.
weaknesses: Necessary: Resolve the POJ-104 evaluation protocol. Section 3.2 and Table 2 specify non-overlapping training, development, and test classes, while Sections 2.3 and 4.2 describe supervised classification into 104 classes. The manuscript does not explain how the classifier predicts unseen classes. If this is actually retrieval, specify the training objective, candidate pool, ranking procedure, and metric definitions. This ambiguity affects the principal results and ablations in Tables 3, 7, and 8.

Necessary: Align the binary-analysis claims with the evaluated inputs. The experiments use LLVM IR generated directly from source, and Figures 7–8 retain informative function names and types. This does not establish performance on stripped executables or IR lifted from them; the footnote describing these representations as trivially interchangeable is inaccurate. Either narrow the claims to the demonstrated LLVM setting or provide evidence for the broader deployment setting.

Necessary: Strengthen the attribution to interpolation. The primary-only model receives 10 pretraining epochs, whereas the full model receives 30 or 70, depending on the task. Section 5.1 asserts convergence of the shorter baseline without presenting supporting learning curves. A comparison under matched training budgets is needed to distinguish interpolation benefits from additional training. Separate linear/nonlinear ablations are also needed if their individual benefits remain claimed. Uncertainty estimates would help interpret the smaller reported gains.

Necessary: Narrow or substantiate the conclusions about human-written comments. Table 7 reports a striking MAF1 decline from 38.19 to 3.06, but comment extraction, handling of missing comments, and whether both conditions use identical programs are insufficiently specified. Length distributions alone do not establish the proposed causes of failure. Document the comparison and investigate the collapse, or restrict the conclusion to the particular raw-comment pipeline tested rather than generalizing about human versus generated comments.

Necessary: Distinguish textual agreement from semantic correctness. Summarization and reverse engineering are evaluated through overlap metrics, exact match, and selected examples, without systematic factuality or execution-based validation. The AnghaBench pipeline generates comments with CodeT5, so the provenance and independence of evaluation summaries also need clarification. Claims about semantic consistency and practical comprehension require corresponding evidence or narrower wording. Table 6 additionally shows that GraphCodeBERT has higher reverse-engineering BLEU-4 than CONTRABIN.

Necessary: Reconcile implementation and reporting inconsistencies. Figure 3 supplies concatenated embeddings to the interpolation network, whereas Equations 8 and 10 specify their sum. The text alternates between arbitrary modality pairs and a fixed binary-versus-source/comment arrangement. Section 3.2 says generation is evaluated on validation data, while Section 4.3 refers to test data. Section 5.1 also mistakes relative percentage reductions for percentage-point changes: 38.19 to 37.40 is a 0.79-point decrease, not 2.07 points. These details impede reliable interpretation and reproduction.

Optional: Shorten the repeated human-learning analogies and present them as motivation rather than established explanations. Comparisons with binary-specific methods would strengthen positioning, but acceptance need not depend on state-of-the-art performance. The unresolved concerns above concern evidential support and clarity, despite the topic having a clear interested audience.
